_comment: Registration for scripts/check-claude-md-budget.py (ADR 0008 row 28, control added #1071).
WHY NOW: #1071 parameterised this script (a positional document and --budget)
so one instrument caps both CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md. The Negative Control rule's
second clause applies to CHANGING an instrument, not only to adding one - widening
a check is exactly where the distinction it draws can silently disappear - so the
control lands in the same commit as the parameter.
WHY THIS GATE NEEDS ONE: it is a gate that lets work THROUGH, a prerequisite of
`make verify`, and nothing downstream re-derives it. A blind version prints the
same 'ok - N/2000 words' line over a document that has doubled.
WHAT THE CAP IS FOR: an always-loaded document is loaded into every session on
its surface, so its size is a tax on every one of them. For AGENTS.md the budget
rejects a specific thing - APPENDING CLAUDE.md's Core Directives block (389
words) to AGENTS.md's content (308), which lands at 697. It does NOT forbid
restating the rules: a document that deletes the Codex-specific content and
pastes the block in its place measures 399 and passes. A count instrument
cannot forbid content, and the semantic property - no sentence in AGENTS.md
explains a Core Directive - stays with review (#1071 post-merge review).
The cases carry CLAUDE.md because that is the default invocation and the one row
28 records. The AGENTS.md parameterisation is exercised by
tests/test_check_claude_md_budget.py, which can vary the budget per case where a
committed case tree carries only one.
limits: Covers the WORD COUNT against a budget, for the default document and budget. It says nothing about whether the real CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md is correct - that is the gate's own run under `make verify` over the real tree - and nothing about the --budget/positional paths, which need a differently-parameterised invocation per case and are covered by tests/test_check_claude_md_budget.py instead.

cases.name: bad-over-budget
cases.why: A CLAUDE.md of 2100 words against a 2000 budget - 100 over. Distinct tokens rather than one repeated word, so the case cannot pass for a reason peculiar to the counter. This is the only failure a word cap exists for; if it scores GOOD the cap is decoration.

cases.name: good-within-budget
cases.why: The same shape at 100 words. Separates a working gate from one wedged at 'fail', which the bad case alone cannot do - and this gate is a prerequisite of `make verify`, so a wedged one blocks every merge.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED, and deliberately NOT the pre-#1071 script. That version carries --root, can be pointed at a case tree, and EXITS 1 on cases/bad-over-budget - it detects the known-bad input, which disqualifies it as an anchor. This is the plausible weaker check instead: confirm the document is present and non-empty and call that within budget - 'it is there' mistaken for 'it is small enough'. It catches a missing or empty file and is blind to one over budget. It MISSES the known-bad input and AGREES with the current gate on the known-good one.
